central_caddy_reload_contract.source_of_truth_before: deploy/caddy/stayconnect-caddy.service was a SINGLE unit shared by both roles, carrying 'ExecReload=/usr/bin/caddy reload --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --force' and 'Description=StayConnect edge proxy (Caddy)'. Central's live unit was hand-written and had NO repository source at all, so a redeploy from the repository would have installed the Edge unit - and its impossible ExecReload - onto Central.
central_caddy_reload_contract.interim_state_from_T0027: T0027 changed the LIVE Central unit to 'ExecReload=/usr/bin/caddy validate ...'. That removed the failure but introduced a worse contract: systemctl reload then reports SUCCESS while the running configuration is untouched. A green result for a no-op is more dangerous than a red one for an impossible operation.
central_caddy_reload_contract.source_of_truth_after: Two role-specific units exist in the repository. deploy/caddy/stayconnect-caddy.edge.service (renamed from the shared file) keeps a working ExecReload, because the Edge Caddyfile leaves the admin API on 127.0.0.1:2019 and reload genuinely applies configuration there. deploy/caddy/stayconnect-caddy.central.service has NO ExecReload at all, so 'systemctl reload' fails immediately with 'Job type reload is not applicable' - the truth, rather than either a quiet failure or a false success. Both units carry the reasoning in their headers, and deploy/caddy/README.md states the contract.
central_caddy_reload_contract.operator_contract: Central: 'caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile' then 'systemctl restart stayconnect-caddy', then verify the ACTIVE configuration rather than assuming the restart applied it. Edge: validate then 'systemctl reload'.

edge_unsupported_host_behaviour.before: After T0027 removed the two Central-only vhosts, the Edge had no route for api.stayconnect.local or admin.stayconnect.local, and Caddy's no-route default is an EMPTY HTTP 200. An uptime check reads that as 'this host serves that name and it is healthy' - misleading in a way the 502 it replaced was not.
edge_unsupported_host_behaviour.after: Both names are declared in deploy/caddy/Caddyfile.edge purely to be refused: a handle block responding 404 with a short explanation, security headers applied, logged to /var/log/caddy/unsupported-host.log. There is NO reverse_proxy in that block and no route to any absent Central service.
